new_statements.quote: In many cases, stress is insensitive to weight; in some languages, stress location is sensitive to morphosyntactic factors. One [Torricelli; Sandaun, PNG] regularly assigns stress to the penultimate syllable, but verbs allow for stress on either syllable of the final foot, resulting in contrasts such as ['te.re] 'chop' and [te.'re] 'howl'. While forms such as the noun ['te.li] 'round thing' would be equally legitimate for a verb, *[te.'li] with final stress is not a possible noun. (Google Books scanned renders the IPA stress mark as an apostrophe.)

new_statements.rule_in_words: Default word stress in One is on the penultimate syllable; in verbs stress is lexically either penultimate or final (either syllable of the word-final foot), giving verb minimal pairs by stress position; nouns never have final stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said in the recovered passage.
new_statements.exceptions: Verbs: stress may fall on either syllable of the final foot (['te.re] 'chop' vs [te.'re] 'howl'); final stress is excluded for nouns. Weight plays no role (passage contrasts One with weight-sensitive systems).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress in citation forms (disyllables cited). 'One' here is Donohue's field language, which he defines elsewhere (Donohue 2000, fn. 1) as the Molmo variety = Molmo One [aun], molm1235 -- not specifically Kabore One.
new_statements.identity_note: The only stress statement found is for 'One' in Donohue's sense, i.e. the Molmo variety (Donohue 2000 fn. 1) = Molmo One [aun], Glottolog molm1235, a sister of Kabore One [onk] kabo1248 inside Central-Northern One. No source states stress for Kabore One (villages Kabore/Abore, Sapin, Kara, Kaye) specifically; Crowther 2001 is the only work with primary Kabore data. The statement should be routed to molm1235 (or to the One cluster onee1245) rather than entered under kabo1248.
